title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: available in the US Department of Defense (DoD) cloud
summary: Held because the briefing asserts that connection deployment cannot enable government-cloud external connections, a distinction Microsoft does not document in the sources checked. The listed control paths, calls, default and licensing are supported; some checklist controls have no table row.

claims.claim: Imported connector data is Customer Data under Microsoft's enterprise terms.
claims.quote: Data imported into your Microsoft 365 services using Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors will be "Customer Data" under the Product Terms, Data Protection Addendum, and Microsoft's enterprise data obligations.

claims.quote: As the data controller, you're solely and exclusively responsible for: a) the Connector Functionality; and b) using the Microsoft 365 Copilot connector in compliance with any third-party rights, licenses, and obligations.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The service description does not describe how government-cloud external connections are enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors government clouds DoD external connections partner connectors enable default switch. Opened service description, deployment-overview and manage-connector. The service description gives the default but no enablement procedure.

claims.claim: Neither connection deployment nor access-permission configuration decides whether external connections are enabled for a government-cloud tenant in the first place.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors government clouds DoD external connections partner connectors enable default switch; Copilot connectors government enable external connections. Opened service description, deployment-overview and manage-connector; none states this separation from deployment.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'Neither control decides' with: 'Microsoft's service description says external connections and partner connectors are not enabled by default for government clouds, but does not describe how they are enabled.' Do not assert that deployment cannot enable them.

claims.claim: All controls that the governance checklist asks administrators to set or check appear in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Assign the AI administrator role', 'Check the identity mapping on the Users tab', 'Schedule full crawls', and 'allow the usdodcentral and usdodeast ranges'. Table: connection deployment, access permissions and user licence assignment only.
claims.fix: The role-assignment, identity-mapping, crawl-scheduling and source-firewall checklist steps have no corresponding controls-table row. Remove these steps from Governance guidance to reconcile the checklist with the existing table; their documented background in Risk assessment and Scope can remain.
